I chose these 10 hypotheses from standard training dynamics, using your 100 single-seed probes as supporting evidence. Most probes changed one hyperparameter from a single base configuration, so each interaction has only a few direct data points. The strongest signals are at the extremes: very strong regularization (alpha high), the learning-rate edges (low and high bands) and very narrow networks (width low).

1. **alpha up when alpha is high → lower.** Raising an already heavy L2 penalty causes severe underfitting. Probe 11 lost about 5–9 points on every dataset.
2. **alpha down when alpha is high → higher.** Relaxing an over-strong penalty should recover accuracy, whereas at small alpha the same edit does almost nothing.
3. **learning_rate_init up when learning_rate_init is low → higher.** At lr ≤ 1.3e-4, Adam underfits within 243 epochs, so a step up helps. Probe 70 was positive on all three datasets.
4. **learning_rate_init down when learning_rate_init is low → lower.** Lowering an already tiny rate makes underfitting worse.
5. **learning_rate_init down when learning_rate_init is high → higher.** At lr ≥ 0.0774 training diverges or collapses, so a step down moves the model back toward a working regime.
6. **depth up when learning_rate_init is high → lower.** Deeper networks are less stable at large step sizes. Probe 47 lost 14.29 points on segment.
7. **depth down when learning_rate_init is high → higher.** Shallower networks train more stably at a high rate. Probe 58 gained 14.29 points on segment.
8. **batch_size up when learning_rate_init is high → higher.** Larger batches reduce gradient noise, which partially rescues unstable high-rate training. Probe 27 gained 14.29 points on segment.
9. **batch_size down when learning_rate_init is high → lower.** Smaller batches add noise that makes high-rate instability worse. Probe 38 lost 14.29 points on segment.
10. **width up when width is low → higher.** Very narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening them helps more than widening an already wide network. Probe 90 supports this.
